claim: The historiographic tradition around Rajasinha I of Sitawaka associates him with conversion to Saivism and the removal of Buddhist monks from Sri Pada in favour of Saiva ascetics; modern scholarship also notes that the Culavamsa's hostile portrayal omits acts attributed to him in defence or patronage of Buddhism, so the episode should not be generalized into an island-wide extinction of Buddhist institutions.
bounded_by: Single academic synthesis built partly on chronicle tradition. Supports a bounded Sri Pada institutional displacement claim and the historiographic caveat; it does not establish island-wide persecution, assassination of monks, or complete collapse of Pali/Sanskrit learning.
notes: Promotes only the defensible core of GF-SAS-18; the stronger museum-panel wording remains unpromoted.
